bicountbrms

Custom brms families for Bayesian modelling of pairs of counts that are positively correlated. Applications include counts recorded by two sources that measure the same quantity, such as two observers, two instruments, or two reporting channels.

The pair (y_1, y_2) is modelled by trivariate reduction, with Poisson components in bipois() (Holgate 1964; Karlis and Ntzoufras 2003) or negative-binomial components in binegbin() (Kirkpatrick and Neale 2016; Kirkpatrick 2022). Each count is the sum of a latent count recorded by both sources, which induces the correlation, and a latent count recorded by that source alone.

The native parameters of the model are the rates and (for negative binomial) dispersions of the three latent components. The model can also be fitted using alternative congruence–bias coordinates, each of which directly represents a quantity of interest when comparing two sources: the midpoint of the two expected counts, the congruence between the two sources, the source bias, and (for negative binomial) the overdispersion of each component. bf_mfd() writes the brms formula in these coordinates, so priors and predictors act directly on the quantities of interest, and summary(fit) reports the posterior of each coordinate. The native parameterisation can be fitted with an ordinary brms formula, in which a predictor can instead act on a single latent component; see Models with predictors in Getting started.

The _partialobs() constructors fit the model when one source has missing values, and the fitted model can impute the missing counts of that source conditional on the recorded counts from the other source.

The core functions

both counts recorded source 1 has missing values
equidispersed (Poisson latent counts) bipois() bipois_partialobs()
overdispersed (negative-binomial latent counts) binegbin() binegbin_partialobs()

Each row of the table is one family. The two constructors of a family share the likelihood and the post-processing methods, and the _partialobs() constructor also takes the observation indicator y1_obs.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("anhsmith/bicountbrms")

Stan and a C++ toolchain are required. On Windows, install Rtools45. Either rstan or cmdstanr works as the brms backend.

Minimal fits

The models below are written in the congruence–bias coordinates with bf_mfd(), which takes one formula for each coordinate (logM, logitf, delta, kappas, kappaxone, and kappaxtwo; see Getting started for their definitions). y_2 is passed to the family as supplementary integer data through vint(), and the Stan function for the family through the stanvars argument. Both are required. brms gives every coordinate a flat, improper prior unless one is set, and Getting started gives a prior for each coordinate.

Paired designs 

library(brms)
library(bicountbrms)

fit <- brm(
  bf_mfd(
    y1 | vint(y2),
    logM      ~ 1,
    logitf    ~ 1,
    delta     ~ 1,
    kappas    ~ 1,
    kappaxone ~ 1,
    kappaxtwo ~ 1
  ),
  family   = binegbin(),
  stanvars = binegbin_stanvars(),
  data     = dat,
  prior    = priors  # one prior for each coordinate; see Getting started
)

Partially paired designs

Where source 1 has missing values, the data need an observation indicator y1_obs, 1 where y_1 was recorded and 0 where it was not. y1 must not be NA, because brms drops any row with a missing response with only a warning. On an unpaired row, the likelihood term does not depend on y1, so y1 can be any integer. We suggest -1, because it cannot be confused with a recorded count:

dat$y1_obs <- as.integer(!is.na(dat$y1))
dat$y1[is.na(dat$y1)] <- -1L

The indicator is passed as the second argument of vint(), and the family and its stanvars are the _partialobs constructors:

fit_po <- brm(
  bf_mfd(
    y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs),
    logM      ~ 1,
    logitf    ~ 1,
    delta     ~ 1,
    kappas    ~ 1,
    kappaxone ~ 1,
    kappaxtwo ~ 1
  ),
  family   = binegbin_partialobs(),
  stanvars = binegbin_partialobs_stanvars(),
  data     = dat,
  prior    = priors
)

To impute y_1 on the rows where it was not recorded, use posterior_predict_y1_given_y2(); see Prediction and imputation.

Documentation

  • Getting started describes one binegbin() analysis from start to finish: simulating data from known parameters, fitting the model in the congruence–bias parameterisation, checking recovery of the generating values, predicting both counts, and comparing the fit with a Poisson model.
  • Partially paired designs fits a model in the congruence–bias parameterisation to simulated data in which source 1 has missing values, and compares the imputed values of y_1, given y_2 and marginal, with values withheld from the model.
  • Prediction and imputation describes the prediction functions and the imputation of y_1 on unpaired rows.
  • The congruence–bias parameterisation has an interactive widget that simulates pairs of counts from one model and shows the congruence–bias and native parameterisations side by side, and gives the equations that convert between the coordinates and the native parameters.
  • The changelog records what each release changed.

A companion package, skellambrms, supplies Skellam, discrete Laplace, and discrete normal families that model d = y_1 - y_2 directly, with optional truncation via resp_trunc().
